pos.personaBrief: No verified possession evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge Wenger's 2005-11 Arsenal were a ball-dominant passing side, consistent with the fan blog's 'retain the ball, and pass it well' and the unverified summary on possession football.

pro.personaBrief: Build-up is a gap axis; from general knowledge the team played out short through Fabregas and line-breaking passes rather than long balls, consistent with the verified 'retain the ball, and pass it well' claim.

est.personaBrief: The 4-3-3/4-2-3-1 (4-2-4 lineage) used box-to-box midfielders 'capable of both being offensive and defensive', and wide players gave 'little cover for our full backs', pointing to fluid, combinative movement rather than fixed zones.

lar.personaBrief: Wide players who did not cover full-backs (verified fan blog) fits inverted attackers drifting inside, with Sagna and Clichy supplying width; the attack ran through the centre.

blo.personaBrief: The fan blog says the system 'requires the team to be able to defend from the front' and that Arsenal were outnumbered in their own half in big games, suggesting a front-foot team that was exposed when it lost the ball; no pressing detail is verified.

mar.personaBrief: No marking detail is verified; from general knowledge Wenger's Arsenal defended zonally, including at set pieces, without tight man-markers.

pla.personaBrief: Wenger kept the same young passing model even without silverware since 2005 and refused to break his project ('You destroy what you have done and created'), showing a commitment to his own identity over adapting to opponents.

res.personaBrief: A trophyless era kept faithful to a stylish, development-led model (no silverware since 2005 per UEFA), which points to valuing how the team plays over pure results.

sis.personaBrief: Midfielders who were trusted to attack and defend, and Wenger's belief in giving young players room ('if you don't play him, you lose him'), point to trusting players' quality and freedom over a rigid system.

jog.personaBrief: The verified emphasis on retaining and passing the ball well, with Song, Diaby, Ramsey and Denilson as technical two-way midfielders, makes technique the priority over physicality.

bas.personaBrief: This is the strongest-evidenced axis: an outfield average age of 23.5 in a CL semi, a League Cup side of about 19, and Wenger's 'you have to make room for them' and 'cannot have a youth policy and suddenly... buy three players [aged] 27'.

lid.personaBrief: People-management is a gap axis; from general knowledge Wenger led through trust and patience with a young group (Fabregas speaks of 'togetherness'), favouring harmony over an iron fist.
